q: Why does inspecting a wooden aircraft call for methods and equipment other aircraft do not need?
evidence: Inspection of wooden structure includes some methods, equipment, and awareness of failure modes which are unique to wooden aircraft.

q: Why are bolt holes a problem in wooden structure?
evidence: Bolt holes in wooden structure provide a vulnerable entry point for moisture.

q: When may permanent tacks replace a hand-sewn seam?
evidence: PERMANENT TACKS MAY BE USED TO SECURE FABRIC AT WING BUTT STRUCTURES IN LIEU OF A HAND-SEWN SEAM AND SHOULD BE OF THE APPROPRIATE LENGTH AND GAUGE, AND MADE OF CORROSION RESISTANT STEEL OR BRASS.

q: What holds reinforcing tape in place before cord lacing or hardware is installed?
evidence: Reinforcing tape should be securely bonded to the fabric surface with dope before cord lacing or installation of hardware.

q: What are nitrate and butyrate dope made from?
evidence: Nitrate dope and butyrate dope are manufactured by treating cellulose, derived from wood pulp or cotton linter with select acids, then dissolving in a blend of solvents and adding plasticizers for flexibility.

q: How large an opening may a doped-on patch repair?
evidence: An opening not over 8 inches in length in any direction, on an aircraft with a Vne speed less than 150 mph, may be repaired with a 2-inch overlapped and doped patch.

q: Why must laminate composition be considered before restoring a part?
evidence: There is a wide variation in the composition and structural application of laminates, and it is essential that these factors be given major consideration when any restoration activities are undertaken.

q: What are the two main classes of plastics?
evidence: Plastics cover a broad field of organic synthetic resin and may be divided into two main classifications – thermoplastics and thermosetting plastics.

q: What is preferred over repairing a badly damaged transparent plastic part?
evidence: Replace, rather than repair extensively damaged transparent plastic, whenever possible, since even a carefully patched part is not the equal of a new section, either optically or structurally.

q: What is the first step before repairing a metal structure?
evidence: Proper identification of the aircraft structural material is the first step in ensuring that the continuing airworthiness of the aircraft will not be degraded by making an improper repair using the wrong materials.

q: What first-aid item belongs where welding is done?
evidence: FIRST-AID KITS. Always keep a special welder’s first-aid kit where it is easily accessible.

q: What does the NDI chapter say about covering every method in detail?
evidence: The field of NDI is too varied to be covered in detail in this Advisory Circular (AC).

q: Which parts deserve magnetic particle inspection?
evidence: Use magnetic particle inspection on any well-cleaned surface that is accessible for close visual examination.

q: What does shearography provide in real time?
evidence: The process now provides a full-field video strain gauge, in real time, over large areas.

q: Why can corrosion be classified by its appearance?
evidence: All corrosive attacks begin on the surface of the metal making the classification of corrosion by physical appearance a convenient means of identification.

q: What is abrasive blasting used for on ferrous metals?
evidence: Abrasive blasting is used for the removal of rust and corrosion and for cleaning prior to painting or plating.

evidence: These bolts are only used in applications subject to shear stress, and are often used as mechanical pins in control systems.

q: What wire are aircraft control cables made from?
evidence: Aircraft control cables are generally fabricated from carbon steel or corrosion-resistant steel wire of either flexible or nonflexible-type construction.

q: Where should engine repair information come from first?
evidence: Consult the manufacturer’s manuals, service bulletins, and instruction books regarding the repair and overhaul, inspection, installation, and maintenance of aircraft engines, for that particular make, model, and type of engine.

q: What determines the wire type used in an ignition harness?
evidence: Aircraft-quality ignition harness is usually made of either medium or hightemperature wire.

q: Why should exhaust system parts never be marked with a lead pencil?
evidence: Inspect exhaust systems frequently to ascertain complete system integrity.

q: Why is propeller vibration troubleshooting difficult?
evidence: Although vibration can be caused by the propeller, there are numerous other possible sources of vibration which can make troubleshooting difficult.

q: What types of landing gear does the chapter cover?
evidence: The landing gear on aircraft may be fixed or retractable.

q: Where should a mechanic stand when servicing a tire?
evidence: When servicing aircraft tires, personnel should stand either in the front or rear of the wheel and avoid approaching from either side of the tire.

q: How is the flotation tube inspection date recorded?
evidence: The date the inspection was completed will be stenciled on the flotation tube at the left of the cylinder.

q: Why must soap be fully removed from washed upholstery?
evidence: Upholstery and/or belts that have been washed may lose some or all of their fire-resistant qualities.

evidence: The removal or addition of equipment results in changes to the center of gravity (c.g.).

q: Where are the weighing procedures for a given aircraft found?
evidence: Weighing procedures may vary with the aircraft and the type of weighing equipment employed.

q: What is being checked in the most rearward weight and balance example?
evidence: O CHECK: MOST REARWARD WEIGHT AND BALANCE EXTREME.

q: What counts as an aircraft's electrical system?
evidence: The term “electrical system” as used in this AC means those parts of the aircraft that generate, distribute, and use electrical energy, including their support and attachments.

evidence: Care should be used in the selection of electrical components to ensure that electrical clearance and creepage distance along surfaces between adjacent terminals, at different potentials, and between these terminals and adjacent ground surfaces are adequate for the voltages involved.

q: Where are more detailed electrical symbols found?
evidence: Only those symbols associated with aircraft electrical and electronic wiring have been listed in general.

q: How are avionics systems checked on the ground?
evidence: There are several methods of ground checking avionics systems.

q: What test equipment must a certificated avionics maintainer have?
evidence: Certificated individuals who maintain airborne avionics equipment must have test equipment suitable to perform that maintenance.

evidence: To accomplish any task in aviation maintenance at least three things must be in evidence.

q: How far back does wood aircraft construction go?
evidence: Wood aircraft construction dates back to the early days of certificated aircraft.
